es_statuses: every barangay has a public ES
ap1.context_use: The ES and JHS presence screens and the spacing screen are published as statuses beside AP1's ratios. The spacing screen counts active public ES schools with no other active public ES within spacing_km_rural (rural barangay) or spacing_km_urban (urban barangay), by straight-line distance, using only points that pass the boundary test S-1 in dim_school_location. None of these enters the classroom review queue
ap1.caveat: The order sets criteria for establishing a school. A barangay without a matched public ES may still be served by a nearby school, and the order's prospective-learner and feasibility criteria cannot be tested with current data, so the screens are for review, not a school shortage or construction need. It gives no ratio of schools to learners or population, so learners per public school and school-age population per public school stay project-defined descriptive measures. The spacing screen uses straight-line distance, not road distance or travel time, and an isolated school is one where the order would allow a new school nearby, not one where a school is needed.

ap2.authority: PIDS Discussion Paper 2025-10, supported by the EDCOM 2 summary
ap2.label: PIDS-style illustrative reported-room screen
ap2.source_note: The paper is preliminary and unedited/unreviewed, and states that the 1:50 definition is for illustration purposes only.
ap2.caveat: The project uses an all-level school total and a broader NSBI instructional-room field, while the paper analyzes congestion by school and education level using BEIS classroom data. This is a transparent review screen, not an exact reproduction, an official DepEd ratio, an RA 7880 shortage calculation, or a construction entitlement.

ap3.authority: DepEd DM-OUHROD-2025-1226 enclosure, reproduced in CALABARZON RM 379, s. 2025
ap3.es_authority: Historical World Bank Philippines Education Note based on older DepEd service standards
ap3.jhs_derivation: 45 maximum learners per class * 4 classes / 5 teachers
ap3.shs_derivation: 40 maximum learners per class * 6 classes / 9 teachers
ap3.priority_use: D-062 BQ composite: the gap of reference teachers over reported teachers, scored as a percentile; never a shortage or entitlement
ap3.caveat: ES 35 is historical context. The memorandum directly publishes JHS 45 and SHS 40 as learners per class, not per teacher. JHS 36 and SHS 80/3 are derived comparisons using the same table's teacher-to-class factors. DepEd applies the staffing process by grade and specialization, so none of these aggregate LGU comparisons is a current national shortage formula, staffing entitlement, or teacher priority rank.

bq.label: Relative review priority against published references, not a shortage
bq.ap1_baseline: median school-age population (5-17, 2024) per public school among assessed LGUs of the same type (city or municipality); no published ratio exists (D-061)

steps.detail: AP1 school-age population per public school against its same-type median; AP2 pooled learners per reported room against 50; AP3 reference teachers (sum of eligible learners / level reference) against reported teachers

steps.formula: 100 * PERCENT_RANK() over the gap, among LGUs with all three gaps
steps.detail: a zero gap scores 0; min-max scores are kept only as a sensitivity check because one extreme value compresses the rest

steps.formula: rank correlation and top-50 overlap without each AP and with min-max scores

oecd_jrc_2008.citation: OECD and European Commission Joint Research Centre (2008). Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators: Methodology and User Guide. OECD Publishing, Paris.
oecd_jrc_2008.used_for: Step 5 normalisation (distance to a reference; ranking/percentile; min-max), Step 6 weighting and aggregation (equal weights, linear aggregation), Step 7 uncertainty and sensitivity analysis (excluding one indicator at a time, alternative normalisation)

fgt_1984.citation: Foster, J., Greer, J. and Thorbecke, E. (1984). A Class of Decomposable Poverty Measures. Econometrica, 52(3), 761-766.
fgt_1984.used_for: the one-sided normalised gap: a value counts only by how far it is past the line, and 0 at or below it

cdc_atsdr_svi_2022.citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention / Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (2024). CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index 2022 Database US: Documentation.
cdc_atsdr_svi_2022.used_for: percentile rank = (rank - 1) / (N - 1), higher means more vulnerable; theme scores are summed and the areas ranked on the result

yoo_choi_2022.citation: Yoo, Y. and Choi, S. (2022). Effects of Top-Down Balanced Development Strategies on Regional Balance: Evidence from Public Big Data in Korea. Sustainability, 14(23), 16221.
yoo_choi_2022.used_for: AP1 indicator: one of the paper's educational indicators is the number of schools per 1,000 school-age population, compared across Korean regions (Table 8); AP1's school-age population per public school is its inverse. The paper sets no cutoff, so it backs the measure but not a baseline
yoo_choi_2022.verification: title, authors, journal and the indicator definition confirmed from the indexed text; Table 8's values not checked

jica_2025.citation: Hirota, K., Dartanto, T. and Ishizuka, F. (eds.) (2025). Addressing Social Infrastructure Needs in Asia: Towards a Pandemic Resilient Society. JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development, Tokyo and Jakarta. ISBN 978-4-86357-117-4.
jica_2025.used_for: supporting context for AP1: the project estimates school infrastructure demand from school-age population projections
jica_2025.verification: title, editors, year and ISBN confirmed from the publisher's listing; the chapter and page that support AP1 were not checked when this entry was written

bq.coverage_rule: an LGU missing any of AP1 to AP3 (90% coverage gate or a NULL ratio) is data_review with no score; missing is never scored as 0
bq.caveat: AP2's 50 is PIDS's illustrative school line applied to the pooled LGU ratio, and AP3's references are historical or derived comparisons (D-059). The composite ranks LGUs for review; it does not estimate a classroom, teacher or school shortage, and AP1 is relative to similar LGUs, not to a standard.
